verdict: TWO INDEPENDENT AXES (entanglement vs magic), confirmed. At q=0 (pure Clifford) the magic M_2 is identically zero across the WHOLE entanglement sweep (max |M_2|=7.6e-06) -- a theorem (Clifford preserves stabilizer states), here measured -- so the monitored substrate traverses the full volume->area entanglement transition WITHOUT generating any phase resource: the encoding/entanglement (cost-sector, p) axis does not touch the phase/magic axis. Entanglement responds to p (S drops by 2.51 from low to high monitoring) and barely to q (spread 0.30); magic responds to q (M_2 rises 3.18 from q=0 to q_max) -- it requires its own non-Clifford knob, which the cost sector never supplies. So the entanglement-transition line (p) and the magic/phase line (q) sit on DIFFERENT axes: the three-axis separation (encoding vs phase) holds from the transition perspective, and Door 2's multicritical 'triple point' would need both knobs. Consistent with the sr-arc finding that contextuality/phase tracks self-reference (magic), independent of the cost sector, and with T2.1 (magic as the phase resource). HONEST SCOPE: small N=8 (the clean entanglement transition is the large-N stim result of phaseF/G; here we need only the DECOUPLING, which N=8 shows); magic is injected as T gates (a phase-sector proxy), and projective measurement can itself suppress magic at large p -- but the q=0 zero-magic-across-the-whole-transition statement is exact and is the load-bearing one.
honesty: N=8 (decoupling, not the clean transition -- that is phaseF/G at large N); magic = T-injection proxy; measurement can suppress magic at large p; the exact, load-bearing statement is q=0 => M_2==0 across the entire entanglement transition.
